R001.text: Fix x∈ℝ^n and t>0. H001 gives positive finite dimensions and H002 permits all derivatives used here. By H004, u·u=1. Differentiation in time, by the ordinary product rule for the finite component sum defining the dot product, gives 2u·u_t=0, hence u·u_t=0. Choose the pointwise scalar a from H005. Then u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu)=a(u_t·u)=0. This uses no derivative or regularity of a.

Twice differentiating u·u=1 in time gives 2|u_t|²+2u·u_tt=0. For an arbitrary coordinate j0∈{1,...,n}, twice differentiating in x_{j0} similarly gives 2|∂_{x_{j0}}u|²+2u·∂_{x_{j0}x_{j0}}u=0. Thus u·u_tt=−|u_t|² and u·∂_{x_{j0}x_{j0}}u=−|∂_{x_{j0}}u|². Generalize j0 over the spatial coordinates. Dot the normality equation for a with u and use |u|²=1. Finite distributivity and the definition of Δ_xu give a=u·(u_tt−Δ_xu)=Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|². The same calculation applies to every scalar satisfying that pointwise equation.

F001 proves the two orthogonality identities at the arbitrary point. By F002 substitute the computed value of a into the pointwise normality equation from H005 to obtain u_tt−Δ_xu=(Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|²)u. The scalar was chosen only at this point and is eliminated; it is not promoted to a regular scalar field. Generalizing x and t proves all the asserted pointwise identities.

R002.text: Fix t0>0 and set J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. Both endpoints are positive and the first is strictly smaller than the second. Apply H006 to these two times to obtain a compact set outside which u=q throughout J.

Choose such a compact C from F001. Compact subsets of finite-dimensional Euclidean space are bounded: for example the increasing family of open boxes with positive integral radii covers C, and a finite subcover puts C in one such box. Enlarging its radius if needed gives a positive radius with strict containment in the open box. This also covers C empty.

Choose R as in F002 and set Q=[−R,R]^n. Its Lebesgue measure is (2R)^n<∞. The complement of compact C is open. On the open set (ℝ^n∖C)×int J the map u is the constant q by F001. H002 implies that all positive-order derivatives vanish on that open set. Thus at interior times e, e_t and the products u_t·u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u), for every j vanish outside C. Products and finite sums of smooth derivatives are continuous; in particular e and e_t are jointly continuous on the original open space-time domain.

At any r∈int J, each spatial function in question is continuous, hence Lebesgue measurable, and bounded on compact Q. Its absolute value is bounded by a finite nonnegative constant times the indicator of Q, since it vanishes outside C⊂Q. The integral of that bound is the constant times (2R)^n, which is finite. This proves absolute integrability of e(·,r), e_t(·,r), u_t·u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u, and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u), for every spatial index j. No interchange of a derivative and an integral is used here.

Since t0∈int J, F004 in particular proves integrability of e(·,t0). Generalize the arbitrary t0 and existentially retain the compatible C,R and their box Q, together with F001–F004, to obtain the full quantified support and integrability assertion. Joint continuity of e and e_t was established in S003 using H002. The energy integral has therefore been proved finite at every positive time, before introducing the finite energy function.

R003.text: Fix t0>0 and take J,C,R,Q from N002 at this t0. The guarded definition E is now available. By H001 and H002, the finite product rule and equality of mixed spatial and time derivatives give, at all x and positive t, e_t(x,t)=2u_t(x,t)·u_tt(x,t)+2Σ_{j=1}^n∂_{x_j}u(x,t)·∂_{x_j}u_t(x,t). The products and e_t are integrable at every positive time by N002.

Set η=t0/4. Then η>0 and [t0−η,t0+η]⊂int J. Joint continuity of e_t from N002 on the compact set Q×[t0−η,t0+η] gives a finite nonnegative upper bound for |e_t| there. Indeed its continuous absolute value has a bounded compact image in ℝ.

Choose B0 from F002. For arbitrary x and 0<|h|<η, apply M004 to the real function r↦e(x,r), with derivative r↦e_t(x,r), on the closed interval whose endpoints are min(t0,t0+h) and max(t0,t0+h). Smoothness gives continuity and the indicated derivative on that interval; all times lie in [t0−η,t0+η]. If a total function on ℝ is required, set it to zero at nonpositive times; this leaves this positive interval and its local derivatives unchanged. For x∈Q, M004 and F002 imply |(e(x,t0+h)−e(x,t0))/h|≤B0. This is the same slope in either ordering of the endpoints. For x∉Q both densities vanish by N002, so the quotient is zero. Thus the uniform dominating function on ℝ^n is B0·1_Q, where 1_Q is one on Q and zero off Q. It is integrable since Q is measurable of finite measure.

Fix an arbitrary sequence hseq:ℕ→ℝ. Temporarily assume L1: for every k, 0<|hseq(k)|<η and hseq(k)→0. Define Fseq(k)(x)=[e(x,t0+hseq(k))−e(x,t0)]/hseq(k). Each Fseq(k) is continuous in x and hence almost everywhere strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure. F003 gives the bound |Fseq(k)(x)|≤B0·1_Q(x) for every k and x. The definition of the time derivative gives Fseq(k)(x)→e_t(x,t0) at every x, because hseq tends to zero through nonzero increments. All Fseq(k) are integrable, by the bound or by integrability of their two densities.

Apply M001 with measurable space ℝ^n, Lebesgue measure, codomain ℝ, sequence Fseq, limit x↦e_t(x,t0), and bound B0·1_Q. F003 and F004 verify all premises. It follows that ∫Fseq(k) dx→∫e_t(x,t0) dx. Since both densities are integrable by N002, linearity of the real Lebesgue integral identifies the left integral with [E(t0+hseq(k))−E(t0)]/hseq(k).

Discharge L1: F005 holds for every sequence of nonzero increments tending to zero and having absolute value less than η. This proves the full punctured limit as the increment tends to zero: otherwise one could choose, in successively smaller punctured neighborhoods of zero, increments whose energy quotients stay a fixed positive distance from ∫e_t(x,t0)dx. Such a sequence tends to zero and lies in that same increment range, contradicting F005. Thus E is differentiable at t0 with E'(t0)=∫e_t(x,t0) dx. Together with F001, and generalization of arbitrary t0, this proves the full asserted differentiability formula and its integrability clauses. Neither the chosen support witnesses nor the test sequence escapes this conclusion.

R004.text: Fix t0>0 and j∈{1,...,n}, and choose compatible J,C,R,Q from N002 at t0. Define g(x)=u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}u(x,t0). It is smooth by H002. It is zero off C by N002. Since the compact C lies in int Q, there is a neighborhood of ∂Q disjoint from C (and if C is empty all these functions are zero everywhere). Therefore g vanishes on a neighborhood of ∂Q. The product rule gives ∂_{x_j}g=∂_{x_j}u_t·∂_{x_j}u+u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u at time t0. All three derivative integrands are integrable by N002.

Let Qrest=[−R,R]^(n−1), and let T(y,z) insert z into coordinate j, keeping the other coordinates in their original order. Set Hfun(y,z)=∂_{x_j}g(T(y,z)). The coordinate permutation identifies Q with Qrest×[−R,R] and Lebesgue integration on Q with integration for the product of Lebesgue measure restricted to Qrest and Lebesgue measure restricted to [−R,R]. This follows from the Cartesian product definition of Euclidean Lebesgue measure: rectangles have the product of their side lengths, invariant under coordinate reordering; that determines this measure. If n=1 the remaining factor ℝ^0 is a singleton with mass one, so the same identification applies. Both restricted measures are finite, hence s-finite. Hfun is continuous and bounded on this compact product; the product measure is finite, so Hfun is integrable there. For each fixed y∈Qrest, z↦g(T(y,z)) is smooth with derivative Hfun(y,z). Its derivative is bounded on [−R,R], hence interval integrable, and its endpoint values are zero by F001.

For arbitrary y∈Qrest apply M003 with codomain ℝ, endpoints −R,R, f(z)=g(T(y,z)), and derivative d(z)=Hfun(y,z). R>0 and F002 give the ordering, continuity, derivative and integrability premises. It follows that ∫_{−R}^{R}Hfun(y,z) dz=g(T(y,R))−g(T(y,−R))=0. Since endpoints have one-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero, the interval integral equals the integral for Lebesgue measure restricted to [−R,R]. Generalize y.

Apply M002 to Hfun with outer measure Lebesgue measure restricted to Qrest and inner measure Lebesgue measure restricted to [−R,R], codomain ℝ. F002 proves product integrability and s-finiteness. The iterated integral is zero by F003. Fubini therefore gives zero for the product integral, and the coordinate identification in F002 gives ∫_Q ∂_{x_j}g dx=0. This holds also in the singleton outer factor when n=1.

By F001 the derivative and both product summands vanish outside Q, so their whole-space integrals equal their integrals over Q. Integrate the product identity in F001, using absolute integrability and linearity. F004 gives 0=∫_{ℝ^n}∂_{x_j}u_t·∂_{x_j}u dx+∫_{ℝ^n}u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u dx, at time t0. Symmetry of the Euclidean dot product gives the asserted identity with ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t on the left. Generalize t0 and j to obtain the asserted integration-by-parts identity, including the integrability clauses.

R005.text: Fix t0>0. N002 proves integrability of e(·,t0) and of all product terms below, so E is the actual finite integral. N003 proves its differentiability and gives E'(t0)=∫e_t(x,t0) dx with e_t=2u_t·u_tt+2Σ_{j=1}^n∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t. Substitute this identity, use linearity and interchange the finite sum and integral (H001 gives a finite dimension), and apply N004 to each j. This yields E'(t0)=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t·u_tt dx−2Σ_{j=1}^n∫_{ℝ^n}u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u dx=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu) dx, all fields evaluated at t0.

By N001 the final integrand in F001 is zero at every x, so E'(t0)=0. Since t0 was arbitrary, N002 and N003 together prove the complete target: e(·,t) is integrable and E is differentiable with E'(t)=0 for every positive t. No time-zero value or limiting assertion is used.

To retain the final conservation statement of the supplied proof, fix s,t>0. If s<t, apply M004 to E and the zero derivative on [s,t]; extend E by zero to nonpositive times solely to match the source's total domain. F002 gives differentiability and hence continuity at all points of this positive closed interval, and derivative zero in its interior. The theorem gives slope zero and therefore E(t)=E(s). If t<s use the same application with the endpoints interchanged, and if s=t equality is immediate. Thus E is constant on (0,∞). This retains exactly the exercise's normalization.

1: # Shared-lemma extraction as a local NL0 revision
2: 
3: ## Scope and position
4: 
5: Apply this procedure at the start of **NL0-to-Lean translation**, before final
6: interface/planning freeze or worker-packet generation. It is not an extra
7: requirement for a task that requests NL0 alone. The input is an existing,
8: versioned NL0, not an invitation to reconstruct its proof.
9: 
10: The operation is proof factoring: move an already supplied local derivation
11: into one shared N/R pair and replace its occurrences by explicit applications.
12: Do not rewrite the whole NL0, regenerate its prose, reprove unchanged results,
13: or seek a stronger/general theorem for speculative future reuse. Reading the
14: existing graph to locate candidates is not a new proof-construction task.
15: If an existing N already exports the needed fact, reuse that node directly.
16: 
17: Use [the revision record](../templates/source-refactoring.md). Preserve the
18: original package and audit as immutable evidence. Write a revised package in
19: a new directory; retain existing IDs and keep the revision identity in the
20: sidecar record. Generated Markdown/diagrams are views, never patch authorities.
21: 
22: ## 1. Locate and qualify candidates without reconstructing NL0
23: 
24: Start with existing node statements, direct inputs, definitions and any
25: available index. Locate repeated subarguments using their mathematical role,
26: objects, formulas or operation names; then inspect the actual candidate spans
27: and the local context they need. Do not commission a new proof or a full prose
28: summary for every node as a discovery method. Text similarity is only a lead.
29: 
30: For each proposed lemma record:
31: 
32: - The complete mathematical statement, all parameters/conditions and proposed
33:   direct input IDs, together with exact old graph pointers or paragraph spans.
34: - The existing derivation to reuse and every occurrence that will consume it.
35:   The derivation must actually supply the proposed statement; a summary label
36:   or a theorem believed true from memory is insufficient.
37: - Identify the baseline revision/old paragraph IDs separately from the current
38:   new producer. A new N's origin label must state the historical/current
39:   distinction; a bare old R number is ambiguous after consumer editing.
40: - The expected avoided repeated work. An occurrence count is not measured
41:   formalization cost and does not by itself establish a speed benefit.
42: - The scope at each occurrence, including bound variables, temporary
43:   assumptions, definition guards and local facts established before the span.
44: 
45: Prefer a statement already justified at the cuts. Do not generalize its domain,
46: change representations, weaken conditions or introduce new mathematics merely
47: to make more occurrences match. If the proposed derivation needs an earlier
48: local calculation, include that calculation with its justified inputs. Never
49: declare an unexported local fact to be an available graph input.
50: 
51: Temporary assumptions stay closed in an implication or other complete
52: proposition; they cannot become H roots. An extraction that moves a witness,
53: choice, definition or binder across a scope boundary needs an explicit account
54: of the values and properties used afterwards. If that account cannot be made
55: locally and clearly, leave the original argument in place.
56: 
57: ## 2. Write the patch boundary before editing
58: 
59: Prepare an edit allowlist for one candidate or one coherent batch:
60: 
61: | Part | Allowed edit |
62: | --- | --- |
63: | New shared theorem | One fresh N and its R producer, with a complete statement and derivation from existing permitted inputs. |
64: | Actual consumers | Replace only the located repeated proof spans by a complete application; adjust direct inputs, citations and application accounting accordingly. |
65: | Necessary local bookkeeping | Update the directly affected binder/reference accounting and generated views. Record every such edit explicitly. |
66: | Everything else | Preserve the existing record content; do not reorder or renumber it as a cleanup. |
67: 
68: Keep the entire frozen specification unchanged: target P, original H, parameter
69: domains, global definitions/notation, logic, pins and E/M source inventories and
70: statements. Preserve all existing N/P statements and every unmodified argument
71: span. New sources, changed hypotheses, new global definitions, removed existing
72: nodes, or a changed old output are outside this fast factoring operation.
73: 
74: Copy an existing derivation rather than writing a new proof route. The new
75: producer may use only its declared inputs, global definitions and legitimate
76: local derivations. It cannot depend on a consumer output or its descendants.
77: Do not split each consumer into additional source nodes around the shared fact.
78: 
79: Each consumer application must state the parameter substitution, which inputs
80: or local proved facts discharge each condition, and the exact conclusion used.
81: Remove a former direct input only if the remaining argument no longer uses it;
82: retain it when it still has a direct role. A shared theorem is never ambient.
83: 
84: If an edit escapes the allowlist, return that candidate to the shortlist or
85: leave it unextracted. A source defect goes through the existing gap procedure;
86: do not turn a reuse optimization into a repair or a new research route.
87: 
88: ## 3. Check structural preservation globally, reasoning locally
89: 
90: Compare canonical JSON records by stable IDs, not only rendered text or changed
91: line numbers. Record before/after hashes and the actual changed fields/spans.
92: Reject any unexplained diff. Check these global mechanical invariants:
93: 
94: - The frozen specification and protected records are unchanged.
95: - All IDs/references resolve; definitions and guards remain available; there
96:   is no cycle or unsupported initial node; every N/P still has one producer.
97: - Every retained node remains in P's dependency closure. Reject the candidate
98:   if it would require deleting or reorganizing unrelated nodes to restore this.
99: - All consumers declare their actual inputs and remain self-contained. Only
100:   the explicit allowlisted nodes/fields have changed.
101: 
102: Run the existing `../scripts/nl0.py check` on the revised graph and specification.
103: Rechecking graph metadata across the package is allowed and inexpensive relative
104: to rereading every mathematical proof. It does not require a new LLM proof of
105: every node, and it does not establish the semantics of a substitution.
106: 
107: Distinguish **review impact** from **dependency status**. The new producer and
108: edited application boundaries need new mathematical review. An unchanged
109: downstream proof whose input statements and conventions are unchanged need not
110: be reconstructed merely because its ancestors have a new producer. Its final
111: acceptance nevertheless depends on the replacement producer being accepted.
112: Until that happens, affected descendants are pending, not newly accepted.
113: 
114: ## 4. Incremental Audit A: review the new proof and the substitution cuts
115: 
116: This is an incremental review procedure under Audit A's mathematical
117: obligations, not permission to weaken source verification or invent a fresh
118: packet replay. The version-bound receipt limitation below is part of the rule.
119: 
120: First inspect the baseline audit and its evidence bindings. Reuse a judgment
121: only for the exact previously reviewed content, context and evidence. Carry
122: FAIL, UNVERIFIED, inaccessible sources and disclosure limits forward. A source
123: file hash proves byte identity, not that an auditor ever inspected the theorem.
124: An unaudited baseline cannot acquire whole-proof acceptance through extraction.
125: 
126: Review the **new N/R in full**: complete statement, exact inputs, argument,
127: dependency accounting, scopes, guards and E/M applications, and the normal
128: fresh packet-only replay requirement. The extracted proof may be copied, but
129: its new closed interface and context must actually be checked.
130: 
131: For **each changed consumer**, review a substitution cut rather than rewriting
132: or replaying its entire old proof by default:
133: 
134: 1. Compare the old derived conclusion at the cut with the instantiated shared
135:    result, including all conditions, quantifiers and semantic conventions.
136: 2. Check that every condition of the shared theorem follows from that consumer's
137:    declared inputs or explicit in-scope local derivations, without extra facts.
138: 3. Check the interface to the untouched continuation: every subsequently used
139:    proposition, object, value and scope remains available with the same meaning.
140:    Equal output text alone cannot establish preservation of a selected witness.
141: 4. Verify the changed direct-input/citation/application accounting. Reuse source
142:    identity evidence only when unchanged; check every new source application.
143: 5. Bind the untouched remainder to its old reviewed bytes and old review
144:    evidence. Record exactly which old checks are inherited and which new checks
145:    cover the patch. Do not relabel this comparison as a new fresh whole-R replay.
146: 
147: If those boundaries do not justify inheritance, mark that candidate
148: `DEFERRED_NOT_LOCAL` and keep the baseline argument. Do not automatically expand
149: to a full-case audit. A separately requested broader review may inspect the
150: specific unresolved node, but is not part of this fast extraction.
151: 
152: Unchanged target/source/definition reviews and proof regions need no new
153: mathematical re-review when their audited content, applicable context and
154: evidence are unchanged. Do not reopen source searches solely because a global
155: graph hash changed. Changes or failures in their evidence invalidate reuse.
156: 
157: The result is a chain: baseline audit + exact revision + actual new reviews.
158: It is not a copied PASS with an updated graph hash. Record actual reviewer
159: exposure; old-review access is appropriate for delta review and cannot be called
160: an independent fresh packet-only review. This procedure authorizes no additional
161: agent or external-service dispatch.
162: 
163: ## 5. Seal or leave the candidate unextracted
164: 
165: Seal only after the allowlist/diff and graph checks pass and the scoped
166: mathematical review is complete. Keep original and revised manifests, patch,
167: location map, old/new evidence, pending findings and measured preparation cost.
168: Stage all candidate edits transactionally; a failed candidate must not replace
169: the accepted baseline. Do not launch formalization workers for an unaccepted
170: source revision or reuse task packets bound to the old graph.
171: 
172: Then finalize and freeze typed interfaces, shared Lean ports and local plans;
173: only afterwards generate worker packets. Shared Lean interface discovery may
174: use this preparation pass, but must not silently mutate the sealed NL0 later.
175: No extraction is a valid outcome; do not manufacture shared lemmas to satisfy
176: the workflow. The work is bounded by the chosen proof regions and patch size,
177: not a universal minute count. Longer time alone is not a mathematical gap.
178: 
179: ## Executable acceptance and review responsibilities
180: 
181: The unchanged parent checker still binds ordinary format-4 audit to the complete
182: graph. `scripts/source_preparation.py` adds a separate incremental record;
183: it never copies old PASS fields into a forged fresh whole-graph audit.
184: Audit B and `workflow.py` both revalidate that record and all underlying evidence.
185: See [commands and the patch contract](integrated-workflow.md).
186: 
187: The initial executable scope is current-v2 source and nonoverlapping consumer
188: paragraph substitutions. Old proposition records/specification, unlisted R
189: records, untouched paragraphs and local fact/assumption lifetimes are protected.
190: Consumer source-application changes can remove obsolete uses, not introduce new
191: external uses. A broader refactor is deferred rather than widening this operation.
192: Multiple proposed edits to one consumer must first be merged into one coherent
193: candidate or left unextracted. Legacy test copies remain development evidence.
194: 
195: Separate three responsibilities:
196: 
197: - A producer reviewer sees only the complete new per-R packet and audits its
198:   conditional mathematics under ordinary Audit A, including actual fresh replay.
199:   Do not ask that packet to establish whole-graph acceptance or old-copy provenance.
200: - A substitution reviewer sees paired before/after consumers, the proposed shared
201:   statement, original derivations and explicit cut contract. `old_derivation`
202:   names THIS consumer's replaced proof; `producer_source_derivation` names the
203:   one original proof used to export the shared lemma. Its supplier may be a
204:   different consumer with a different final goal. Compare the common intermediate
205:   conclusion, not equality of those final goals. Check existing-proof
206:   factoring, each condition, exact supplied conclusion, continuation and accounting.
207:   This is delta review with baseline access, not fresh whole-consumer replay.
208: - Python checks canonical fanout, edit scope, graph validity, immutable evidence,
209:   the exact coverage partition and inherited acceptance/qualifications. It does
210:   not judge natural-language mathematics or authenticate a dishonest reviewer.
211: 
212: Internal N applications are direct inputs, paragraph citations and explicit prose;
213: the parent's `applications` source records remain E/M-only. Do not invent an N
214: source-application record to satisfy a reviewer. A prose citation without a real
215: substitution is not successful factoring. Derivation labels and fanout guesses
216: from a model are leads, not canonical graph facts.
217: 
218: Each cut review binds the exact supplied packet hash. Retain the binding from
219: the generated template and verify it during acceptance. Reusing an actual old
220: review after a record-only change requires identical canonical mathematics and
221: byte-identical actual reviewed packets; preserve its verdicts, notes, evidence
222: and original cost, and disclose that no new mathematical review occurred.
223: 
224: `INCREMENTAL-AUDIT-A-PASSED` requires a passing current baseline plus all actual
225: new producer/cut reviews. Missing/failed baseline checks remain inherited and
226: yield development-only local review. Every later consumer acceptance still
227: depends on the new producer; unchanged input statements and context permit
228: inheriting the old conditional argument without rereading it mathematically.
229: No fixed completion-time threshold makes a candidate worthwhile or incorrect.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
value.conclusion: For every t>0, e(·,t) is absolutely Lebesgue integrable on ℝ^n, E is differentiable at t, and E'(t)=0. In addition E(s)=E(t) for all s,t>0; no assertion at time zero is made.

2: 
3: Audit A's shared section is the mathematical authority. The policy is
4: mathematical-background-v2-1. Ordinary mathematics is reviewed in NL0; exact
5: Mathlib implementation is resolved in nl02lean.
6: 
7: ## Eligibility and record
8: 
9: A note records a correct, routine local step with actual available premises,
10: no new hypothesis, no missing project lemma and no new core proof route.
11: Give id (BG001 etc.), kind (elementary or mathematical), at (an existing
12: /inference/argument/N/text pointer), fact (precise mathematical statement),
13: grounds ([{location,reason}] for real available conditions), and justification
14: (actual mathematical reasoning). A familiar name alone is insufficient.
15: Non-native notes have no source field or claim of a verified Lean declaration.
16: The optional record_background_note tool saves a checkpoint; a complete review
17: may submit all its notes in one artifact without separate tool calls.
18: 
19: For example, continuity of a sum follows from the supplied continuity of the
20: functions and continuous addition on their actual codomain. Check those
21: conditions mathematically. The reviewer need not call Lean or identify
22: Continuous.add before judging that routine step.
23: 
24: Substantive missing arguments, changed quantifiers, missing witness existence,
25: unsupported limit exchanges and uncertain external statements remain blocking.
26: The controller validates structure and local pointers; it never decides that
27: a mathematical fact is true or routine. An actual independent reviewer owns
28: that decision and may return FAIL or UNVERIFIED.
29: 
30: ## Handoff
31: 
32: The immutable author graph and hash-bound review notes jointly describe the
33: accepted mathematical proof. The format-4 receipt is not a format-3 verified native
34: background policy. Explicit native mathlib notes can still be inspected only
35: with their complete matching pinned evidence; they are optional, not a new
36: requirement for routine mathematical notes.
37: 
38: Normal translation uses node_local_reference. Notes travel with their own
39: paragraphs and do not become additional premise ports. Workers find appropriate
40: library declarations or prove auxiliary facts with their actual conditions.
41: The interface author chooses shared representations, not every local tactic
42: or implementation lemma in advance. Every required fact must eventually be
43: established in checked Lean. No note is an axiom or a new external E.

45: The source supplement hash and exact notes are bound in the interface contract,

1: # Audit A: mathematical review in Yui
2: 
3: <!-- yui-nl0-acceptance:begin -->
4: ## Shared mathematical acceptance requirements
5: 
6: Contract version: `yui-nl0-audit-a-2`.
7: 
8: The author and independent auditor use this same mathematical standard. NL0
9: reviews a complete natural-language proof and necessary mathematical detail.
10: Specific Lean declarations, signatures, representations and proof tactics are
11: implementation work for nl02lean, not prerequisites for ordinary NL0 review.
12: The following grouped criteria replace V1's ten separate per-R report rows.
13: 
14: | ID | Review group | Author evidence group | Requirement |
15: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
16: | `target` | package | original_context_note | Preserve the complete original theorem, every original H, quantifier, domain, normalization and supplied core proof route. A parameter or definition cannot hide a hypothesis or desired conclusion. |
17: | `definitions` | package | declaration_check | Define mathematical objects and notation sufficiently for their actual uses. Check types, dependencies, construction guards and legitimate local introductions. A definition grants no unproved property. |
18: | `sources` | package | original_context_note | Check complete E statements, primary-source identity, context and conditions under the source policy. An explicitly selected native M retains its bound signature checks; authors need not introduce M nodes for ordinary mathematical background. Unavailable originals remain disclosed UNVERIFIED source assumptions. |
19: | `structure` | package | original_context_note | Verify the actual AND dependency graph, unique producers, absence of cycles and faithful exported statements. Retain every original H and disclose unused H. Internal results are proved, never new roots. |
20: | `statement_closure` | closure | output_notes | Inputs and output state the mathematical content, objects, domains, quantifiers and conditions their consumers need. Check actual object occurrences and definitions. No missing identification can be supplied by an absent producer proof or a paper equation number. |
21: | `dependency_closure` | closure | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Check direct input use, earlier local facts, witness existence and proper discharge of assumptions. No circular dependency, future fact or escaped local object is allowed. Mathematically checked routine background may supplement the packet without prior native lookup. |
22: | `argument` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Verify the complete implication and every output clause at ordinary rigorous mathematical granularity, including material limiting operations, domains and regularity. Compress correct routine reasoning; locate a real gap rather than requiring a transcript of elementary steps. |
23: | `applicability` | inference | source_application_check | Check actual instantiations and all material premises of invoked E/M or routine background facts, with grounds in inputs or earlier local derivations. Required bridges are proved. A familiar theorem name or a proposed Lean tactic supplies no mathematical justification. |
24: 
25: ### Scope and mathematical boundary
26: 
27: Global review owns target/H fidelity, definitions, source statements and graph
28: consistency. Each local reviewer owns the conditional implication at its R
29: node. Conditional packet replay has a different input boundary: these statements are conditional premises.
30: The local reviewer does not re-prove an input N or re-audit its source paper;
31: the graph and that producer's review establish those separate obligations.
32: Conversely, an input N exports only its full statement, not unexported facts
33: from the producer's body. The fifth local criterion, packet_replay, assesses
34: sufficiency under this exact boundary. The controller records execution
35: identity and exposure independently of the mathematical judgment.
36: 
37: Review correctness rather than the number of displayed lines. Ordinary valid
38: textbook compression is allowed. Material missing hypotheses, witnesses,
39: constructions, scope discharges or core arguments are not implementation gaps.
40: Return them for located author repair and fresh review. No theorem needs to be re-proved
41: when its legitimate mathematical source and actual application suffice.
42: 
43: The domain-neutral elementary-language-4 profile retains equality, supplied
44: definitions, finite arithmetic/order reasoning and finite sums. It is syntax
45: and elementary calculation policy, not a subject vocabulary or theorem list.
46: Objects from any field use problem parameters, D definitions or scoped locals.
47: Neither an author-written calculation list nor a familiar symbol adds a theorem.
48: 
49: ### Mathematical background: mathematical-background-v2-1
50: 
51: A reviewer may positively assess a routine, local mathematical fact without
52: first finding its Mathlib declaration. Record its precise mathematical
53: statement, actual argument location, available condition grounds and a short
54: mathematical justification in a background note. Use kind mathematical for an
55: ordinary background result and elementary for a useful elementary completion.
56: This is an actual mathematical judgment, not a future TODO or a claim of
57: native verification. Do not record every algebraic operation.
58: 
59: Eligibility requires a correct standard local step with all premises already
60: available, no new H and no substantial new core proof or changed route.
61: Important external tools remain explicit E inputs; a missing project result
62: or uncertain source cannot be waived as background. If an explicitly supplied
63: native mathlib note is retained, its full bound evidence is still validated.
64: No field-specific whitelist determines eligibility.
65: 
66: The accepted authority is immutable author NL0 plus its hash-bound mathematical
67: review supplement. It is a natural-language audit under the mathematical-background policy, not a
68: detailed-NL0 format-3 native-background receipt. At nl02lean, workers must discharge all necessary
69: facts by actual Lean proofs or checked library use; a note never becomes an
70: unproved H, axiom or extra external assumption. The exact implementation may
71: differ while preserving the mathematical meaning.
72: 
73: ### Actual review and result qualification
74: 
75: Independent reviewers assess the actual content; schema validation does not
76: prove mathematics. An unexamined item remains unread/read. A mathematical
77: uncertainty is assessed UNVERIFIED, not PASS. Missing or conflicting assessments
78: block acceptance. Ordinary source-access deferral follows the conditional-source
79: policy and must appear in final warnings; it cannot yield unqualified PASS.
80: 
81: Use short located reasons for straightforward PASS items and enough detail to
82: make a defect or uncertainty actionable. Avoid duplicate explanations across
83: criteria. A concise report still covers every required mathematical check.
84: Do not read author self-check notes, old verdicts, other R proof bodies, other
85: case results or personal proof skills to manufacture independent approval.
86: <!-- yui-nl0-acceptance:end -->
87: 
88: ## Execution protocol
89: 
90: 1. Freeze the original problem, spec and NL0. A separate fresh global reviewer
91:    reads the exhaustive global-overview.json, relevant canonical content and
92:    source evidence. Review each D and selected E/M; the overview is data, not
93:    an assessment. Do not infer absence from a partial page.
94: 2. Complete global source/graph review before dispatching local R reviews.
95:    Up to the explicitly confirmed N independent R reviewers work concurrently.
96:    Each receives only its own packet and mathematical-NL0 rules. Review full arguments,
97:    actual applications and definitions; input N statements are conditional.
98: 3. Prefer one complete artifact with an explicit coverage map. Use
99:    record_review_item and read_review_progress only for useful checkpoints.
100:    record_background_note is optional; a complete artifact may include its
101:    actual notes directly. Batch reading several declared fragments is available.
102: 4. Each local report has inference, packet_sha256, verdict, notes, checks,
103:    findings and optional background_notes. The checks map contains exactly
104:    statement_closure, dependency_closure, argument, applicability, packet_replay.
105:    Each row has verdict, notes and resolving packet locations. E applications
106:    additionally retain actual binding, per-hypothesis, conclusion and bridge
107:    assessments; this is mathematical applicability, not a Lean API inventory.
108: 5. Global reports have target_review, definition_reviews, source_reviews,
109:    structure_review and findings. Each E adds citation_checks for
110:    literature_identity, result_location, statement_fidelity,
111:    context_completeness, version_and_eligibility. Inaccessible primary text
112:    leaves blocked checks UNVERIFIED while remaining assessment continues.
113: 6. A blocking finding needs its actual location, explanation and a short exact
114:    quotation from that location. Preserve the defect and untouched coverage.
115:    Return located mathematical repairs to the author; review changed scopes
116:    independently. Do not resample a mathematical rejection or silently erase it.
117: 7. The collector checks complete coverage, consistency, exact bytes and actual
118:    independent execution before producing the audit-format-4 receipt.
119:    Old detailed-NL0 format-3 receipts are not silently upgraded. Inherited format-4 judgments retain
120:    their original source/rule hashes, exposure and costs.
121: 
122: ## Sources, scopes and final handoff
123: 
124: Use [external theorem review](external-theorems.md) and
125: [conditional sources](conditional-sources.md) for source identity, exact
126: statements and warnings. Reuse adequate original text; several theorem uses
127: may share one staged readback. Each application still discharges its own
128: premises. No successful download or guessed Mathlib availability is approval.
129: 
130: Use [logical rules](logical-rules.md) for local scopes and
131: [background notes](background-notes.md) for the mathematical supplement.
132: The ordinary complete result remains relative to explicit E assumptions.
133: An inaccessible E original permits only a source-qualified result. Translation
134: retains this exact audit and supplement until reviewed mathematical changes
135: invalidate affected scopes. Typed interfaces, native checking, standalone
136: assembly and independent semantic Audit B are separate later gates.
137: 
138: ## Paywalled or inaccessible primary text
139: 
140: Follow [conditional sources](conditional-sources.md). Preserve the complete
141: secondary statement and actual access evidence; unavailable source checks
142: stay UNVERIFIED. Continue other work only with an explicitly qualified source
143: assumption, and report warn.json/warn.md. No unqualified full PASS is granted.
